name: The Goldilocks Principle: Optimal Stimulation Across Modalities
short_description: Cross-modal inverted-U preference curves arising from prediction error optimization within metabolic efficiency windows. The unifying mechanism behind Berlyne's Wundt curve, Kaplan's preference matrix, and domain-specific comfort zones across visual, thermal, acoustic, temporal, and social dimensions of architecture.

components.name: Visual Complexity Optimum
components.description: Fractal dimension D approx 1.3 produces maximal processing fluency via V1/V2 efficient coding. Luminance contrast ratio 1:7-1:15 for aesthetic range. Visual rhythm scaling at 1/f^beta (beta approx 2.6). Fractal complexity and luminance contrast are synergistic: optimal fractal D with optimal contrast ratio produces greater preference than either alone.

components.name: Thermal Comfort Optimum
components.description: Adaptive neutral = 0.31 x T_running_mean + 17.8C. Comfort zone +/-1C; positive alliesthesia (thermal delight) at +/-1-3C when directionally corrective; tolerance +/-3-5C; discomfort beyond +/-5C. Person-dependent via running-mean outdoor temperature expectation.

components.name: Acoustic Comfort Optimum
components.description: Peak pleasantness at 50-60 dB LAeq. Below 45 dB: boring/unsettling. Above 70 dB: aversive. Natural sound content (birdsong, water) shifts optimum upward by +5-10 dB via biophilic reward. Mechanical sound content (traffic, HVAC) shifts optimum downward. ISO 12913 soundscape framework.

components.name: Temporal Variation Optimum
components.description: Light variation: 0.01-2.0 cycles/min optimal engagement; amplitude 8-35% of mean luminance. Architectural promenade: optimal threshold density along movement path — too many rapid compression-release thresholds produce fatigue, too few produce boredom. Light variation and spatial thresholds are synergistic: temporal light changes coordinated with spatial transitions amplify the promenade experience.

components.name: Social Density Optimum
components.description: Optimal range: 3-5 simultaneous social modes supported by spatial configuration. Dunbar saturation threshold: monitoring cost exceeds benefit when >6 conversational groups occupy the visual field. Below 2 modes: social isolation/loneliness. Person-dependent via introversion-extraversion trait.

components.name: Cognitive Complexity Optimum
components.description: Environmental complexity for creativity: moderate novelty promotes divergent thinking via exploratory processing style; excessive novelty overwhelms working memory and collapses to convergent/defensive processing. The environmental Goldilocks zone for creativity has different optima than for comfort — creativity requires higher PE than relaxation but lower PE than stress.

scope_conditions: Applies to neurotypical adult populations; optima may differ for neurodivergent individuals (e.g., sensory sensitivity in autism shifts optima leftward)
Assumes steady-state exposure; transient exposure may not reach equilibrium preference
Cross-modal interactions (e.g., thermal comfort shifting visual complexity tolerance) are documented but not yet fully quantified
Cultural and experiential history shifts optima via IE-DPT prior expectations
key_references: Berlyne, D.E. (1971). Aesthetics and psychobiology. Appleton-Century-Crofts.
Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature. Cambridge University Press.
Taylor, R.P. et al. (2011). Front. Hum. Neurosci., 5, 60.
de Dear, R.J. & Brager, G.S. (1998). ASHRAE Transactions, 104(1), 145-167.
Vessel, E.A. et al. (2012). Front. Hum. Neurosci., 6, 66.
Wundt, W. (1874). Grundzüge der physiologischen Psychologie.
design_implications: Visual complexity: target fractal dimension D = 1.2-1.5 in surface textures, facade patterns, and interior finishes. Use 1/f scaling in spatial rhythm (window spacing, column rhythm, material transitions).
Luminance: target global contrast ratio 1:7 to 1:15 for aesthetic spaces; CV of luminance 0.5-1.5 for comfort; permit CV > 1.5 for dramatic/awe spaces only with bright zone < 20% visual field.

Thermal: design for adaptive neutral +/-1C as the primary comfort target; allow +/-3C excursions only when directionally corrective (warm after cold exposure, cool after heat). Avoid uniform thermal environments — mild thermal variation engages positive alliesthesia.

Acoustic: target 50-60 dB LAeq for restorative spaces; incorporate natural sound sources (water features, vegetation rustling) to shift pleasantness upward. Maintain speech privacy (STI < 0.20) in individual work zones.

Temporal: vary lighting at 0.01-2.0 cycles/min to maintain engagement without flicker annoyance. In circulation sequences, space compression-release thresholds to allow recovery (the promenade principle).
Social: configure spaces to support 3-5 simultaneous social modes. Avoid layouts that force >6 conversational groups into a single visual field (Dunbar saturation).
General: the optimum is person-dependent — provide controllability so occupants can adjust toward their personal optimum. Spaces with higher controllability have wider effective Goldilocks zones.

visual_complexity_d.source: Taylor et al. 2011; Vessel et al. 2012

confidence_intervals.overall_note: Effect sizes are domain-specific; the cross-modal universality claim is supported at d = 0.35-0.52 per domain
